summary: [para 3] 3. As disputes arose between the parties due to the failure of the Respondent AP Discoms to make the payments to LKPL for finance and procurement of Naphtha payable upto September 2001, and the efforts to settle the same amicably, was not responded to by the Respondents, LKPL issued notice on 26.3.2004, nominating Justice B.P. Jeevan Reddy, as its arbitrator and requested the Respondents to nominate their arbitrator. As the Respondents failed to settle the disputes through negotiation or arbitration, LKPL filed an application before the Hon’ble Andhra Pradesh High Court (AA No. 31/2004) for the appointment of an arbitrator. However, the Hon’ble High Court disposed of the said application on 18.3.2009, granting liberty to LKPL to approach the Andhra Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission (APERC) for appropriate relief. Accordingly, LKPL filed O.P. No. 42/2009 before the APERC, seeking the reliefs (b) to (d), as in para 1 above. However, the APERC, in other similar petitions vide order dated 13.6.2011, dismissed the said Petition holding that the period spent by [¶] (viii) LKPL has bonafidely and in accordance with the dispute resolution mechanism provided in the PPA, pursued its remedy to recover the finance and procurement costs payable under the provisions of the PPA. It is a settled law that in computing the period of limitation, the time during which the Petitioner has been prosecuting with due diligence another proceeding should be excluded. Since LKPL had invoked the dispute resolution mechanism as early as 8.9.2003, pursued arbitration in terms of the PPA, and thereafter approached the Hon’ble High Court, the objection of the Respondent Discoms that the claims pertaining to the period prior to September 2001 are barred by limitation is wholly misconceived. Accordingly, the Respondent Discoms remain liable to reimburse the finance and procurement costs for the period up to September 2001. [¶] (xv) Article 5.2 of the PPA prescribes the mandatory procedure for submission of monthly tariff bills for capacity and energy charges. A plain reading of Article 5.2 makes it abundantly clear that all monthly energy bills must be duly supported by documentary proof of actual expenditure incurred. Contrary to this contractual requirement, LKPL has sought reimbursement of finance and procurement charges for the period from June 2000 to August 2001 without furnishing any proof of actual payment. In this context, reliance is placed on the judgment of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in Tata Iron & Steel Co. Ltd. v. Union of India (Civil Appeal No. 6962 of 2000, decided on 30.11.2000), wherein it was categorically held that the term “reimburse” necessarily implies repayment or restoration of an amount already paid or expended, and therefore presupposes proof of prior payment. [¶] company, including reimbursement of Finance and Procurement Costs not incorporated into monthly bills. Accordingly, LKPL issued such Supplementary Bills in terms of Article 5.5, claiming reimbursement under Article 3.3 of the PPA for the period from 22.6.2000 to 10.08.2001, amounting to Rs. 10.79 crore, along with interest of Rs. 10,90,92,073 up to the date of filing the petition, and further interest pendente lite and future interest at the Late Payment rate prescribed under Article 5.11 of the PPA.
